## 1B.4 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** The 2024 record shows **some genuine de-escalation and nonproliferation signaling**, but **little evidence of a broader arms-control or inspection agenda**. Marcos supported incident-management arrangements and denuclearization statements in good faith, while his security posture still leaned on deterrence and allied military activity.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [US, China must engage in meaningful dialogue to maintain strategic stability, limit nuclear arms build-up - PBBM](https://pia.gov.ph/press-releases/us-china-must-engage-in-meaningful-dialogue-to-maintain-strategic-stability-limit-nuclear-arms-build-up-pbbm/) — Philippine Information Agency / Presidential Communications Office, 2024-03-05 | Marcos explicitly called for strategic stability, limits on nuclear arms build-up, and broader nuclear-disarmament discussion. This is the clearest 2024 evidence of support for nonproliferation and disarmament principles. | `1B.4`, `1B.2` |
| E2 | Favorable | [PH, US, Japan affirm commitment to Korean Peninsula denuclearization, warn Russia on nuclear weapon use vs. Ukraine](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-us-japan-affirm-commitment-to-korean-peninsula-denuclearization-warn-russia-on-nuclear-weapon-use-vs-ukraine/) — Presidential Communications Office, 2024-04-12 | Marcos joined a trilateral statement affirming denuclearization and warning against nuclear weapon use in Ukraine. This is direct support for disarmament and anti-nuclear-norm enforcement. | `1B.4`, `1B.2` |
| E3 | Favorable | [PH, Viet Nam sign agreements on rice trade, agriculture, SCS incident prevention and management](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-viet-nam-sign-agreements-on-rice-trade-agriculture-scs-incident-prevention-and-management/) — Presidential Communications Office, 2024-01-30 | Marcos’s Vietnam visit produced an agreement on South China Sea incident prevention and management, plus coast-guard maritime cooperation. This is a concrete de-escalation agreement and one of the best fits for “supported agreements in good faith.” | `1B.4`, `1B.3`, `1B.1` |
| E4 | Favorable | [PH, China agree to 'calmly deal' with incidents in S. China Sea](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217166) — Philippine News Agency, 2024-01-18 | The DFA said both sides agreed to calmly deal with incidents, improve maritime communication mechanisms, and avoid escalation. This is practical support for de-escalation and communication safeguards. | `1B.4`, `1B.3`, `1B.1` |
| E5 | Favorable | [We’re ordered not to be provoked by China’s aggressive actions in WPS - PCG](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/were-ordered-not-to-be-provoked-by-chinas-aggressive-actions-in-wps-pcg/) — Presidential Communications Office, 2024-05-04 | A PCG official said personnel were ordered not to be provoked and to maintain professionalism. This supports the claim that Marcos’s side was trying to preserve restraint while agreements and channels were in place. | `1B.4`, `1B.3` |
| E6 | Favorable | [PBBM salutes troops in dangerous Ayungin resupply mission](https://mirror.pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-salutes-troops-in-dangerous-ayungin-resupply-mission/) — Presidential Communications Office, 2024-06-23 | Marcos praised Western Command troops for “the greatest restraint” during a violent resupply mission. This is evidence that he rewarded disciplined de-escalation behavior rather than retaliation. | `1B.4`, `1B.3`, `1B.1` |
| E7 | Mixed, limited support | [Marcos rejects use of water cannons to retaliate vs. Chinese vessels](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1224081) — Philippine News Agency, 2024-05-06 | Marcos said the Philippines would not use water cannons and had no intention of attacking with offensive measures. This is de-escalatory, but it is not arms control or inspection policy in the formal sense. | `1B.4`, `1B.3`, `1B.1` |
| E8 | Critical / limiting context | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) — Reuters, 2024-03-05 | Balikatan 2024 moved toward islands facing the South China Sea and Taiwan and added cyber/information-warfare elements. This does not negate the de-escalation items above, but it shows Marcos was not pursuing a broad arms-control or demilitarization line. | `1B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.3` |
| E9 | Critical / limiting context | [Philippines holds drills with allies after South China Sea confrontation](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/united-states-japan-philippine-conduct-maritime-exercises-in-south-china-sea-3758253) — Reuters, 2024-12-05 | After another confrontation with Beijing, Manila held maritime drills with the U.S. and Japan inside its EEZ. This shows continued deterrence and alliance signaling, which is not what a strong arms-control or disarmament agenda looks like. | `1B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.3` |

### Synthesis

- **Strongest positive evidence:** Marcos backed at least one **formal incident-prevention arrangement** and made explicit **nonproliferation / denuclearization statements** in 2024.
- **Strongest limiting evidence:** The year still featured **allied military drills and deterrence-heavy signaling**, so this was not a broad arms-control presidency.
- **Search gap:** I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Marcos personally pursued a new **arms-control treaty, inspection regime, or disarmament agreement** beyond the denuclearization statement and South China Sea de-escalation mechanisms. The evidence is real, but narrow.

**Working judgment for 1B.4:** **Partial yes.** Marcos supported **de-escalation and nonproliferation language in good faith**, but there is **no strong evidence of a broader arms-control or inspection agenda** in 2024.
